title: Coherent rational coefficient comparison datum
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $T$ be noetherian, finite dimensional, with $\ell$ invertible. A coefficient comparison datum on $T$ means the following tuple; it asserts no existence. For every finite $E\subset\Omega$, it supplies equivalences of the integral full categories identified by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] and of their raw rationalizations [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. The integral underlying functor is restriction along the quotient-normalized completed-coefficient isomorphism. The rational equivalence fixes integral objects and sends each pure tensor $e\otimes f$ to the same scalar and integral map; it is additive and exact in both directions, and its shift comparison is the localization of the canonical exact restriction-of-scalars shift. For every inclusion $E\subset L$, there is an ordinary tensor transport fixed on all tensor generators and an integral scalar comparison whose complex-localization equation is the specified quotient-map completion chain map of [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison], with zero shifted-product component and the canonical derived counits. Its rationalization is a coherent morphism of the actual scalar systems [lem-weil-scalar-extension-composition], [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]; its inverse is the scalar comparison $j$. The morphism satisfies the scalar associator cocycle, including identity inclusions, and commutes with shifts. Finally the datum contains an additive exact equivalence, exact also in the reverse direction, from the literal pair category [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] to [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category]. Its functor is the functor of this stage-system morphism: it preserves the field label, applies the finite equivalence, and conjugates a common-stage map by the two scalar comparisons. Its shift components are those induced by the finite-stage components. On every common-field representative it preserves multiplication by every element of that field, viewed in $\Omega$. No Karoubi completion occurs.
